"A Mini Shai-Hulud Has Appeared": Bun-Based Stealer Hits SAP @cap-js and mbt npm Packages

Snyk
2026-04-29 10 use cases 6 techniques 6 kill-chain phases detected

A new npm supply chain attack self-branded "Mini Shai-Hulud" compromised four SAP-ecosystem packages on April 29, 2026. Snyk has live advisories. Here's the technical breakdown, IOCs, and what to do.

Mini Shai-Hulud npm preinstall chain: node setup.mjs → bun execution.js AIInstallation High
Hunts the install-time execution chain unique to the @cap-js/* and mbt npm compromises: an npm/yarn/pnpm preinstall script spawning `node setup.mjs`, which in turn spawns `bun execution.js`. The article documents this exact two-stage handoff (setup.mjs is a 4.5KB Bun loader that invokes `bun execution.js` to run the 11.6MB obfuscated stealer). Rationale: Uses the article-named filenames `setup.mjs` and `execution.js` together with the documented parent-child chain (npm preinstall → node → bun). Both filenames are unique to this campaign per Snyk's diff between mbt 1.2.47 (clean) and 1.2.48 (malicious), and the two-stage handoff is byte-identical across all four compromised packages. Cross-checked against: • https://snyk.io/blog/bun-based-stealer-hits-sap-cap-js-mbt-npm-packages/ • https://www.stepsecurity.io/blog/mini-shai-hulud-attack-cap-js-mbt-npm-supply-chain-compromise • https://socket.dev/blog/mini-shai-hulud-cap-js-mbt-supply-chain • https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1195/002/
ATT&CKT1195.002 T1059.007 T1546.016
Data sourcesEndpoint.Processes
DeviceProcessEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(7d)
| where (FileName in~ ("node.exe","node") and ProcessCommandLine has "setup.mjs"
         and InitiatingProcessFileName in~ ("npm.cmd","npm","npm-cli.js","yarn.cmd","yarn","pnpm.cmd","pnpm","node.exe","node"))
   or (FileName in~ ("bun.exe","bun") and ProcessCommandLine has "execution.js")
| where AccountName !endswith "$"
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, AccountName,
          Parent = InitiatingProcessFileName,
          ParentCmd = InitiatingProcessCommandLine,
          Child = FileName,
          ChildCmd = ProcessCommandLine,
          ChildSHA256 = SHA256,
          ChildPath = FolderPath
| order by Timestamp desc
let _PreinstallChain = ImProcessCreate
    | where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
    | where ActorUsername !endswith "$"
    | where (TargetProcessName endswith "node.exe" or TargetProcessName endswith "/node")
        and TargetProcessCommandLine has "setup.mjs"
        and (ParentProcessName has_any ("npm","yarn","pnpm") or ParentProcessName endswith "node.exe" or ParentProcessName endswith "/node");
let _BunPayload = ImProcessCreate
    | where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
    | where ActorUsername !endswith "$"
    | where (TargetProcessName endswith "bun.exe" or TargetProcessName endswith "/bun")
        and TargetProcessCommandLine has "execution.js";
union _PreinstallChain, _BunPayload
| project TimeGenerated, DvcHostname, ActorUsername,
          ParentProcessName, ParentProcessCommandLine,
          TargetProcessName, TargetProcessCommandLine, SHA256
| order by TimeGenerated desc
title: Mini Shai-Hulud npm Preinstall Bun Loader Execution
id: 7a3c4d12-8e6f-4b1a-9f2b-3d5e9a6c1e7f
description: Detects the install-time execution chain of the Mini Shai-Hulud npm supply chain attack (@cap-js/db-service, @cap-js/sqlite, @cap-js/postgres, mbt) where a preinstall hook runs `node setup.mjs` which downloads Bun and executes `bun execution.js`.
references:
  - https://snyk.io/blog/bun-based-stealer-hits-sap-cap-js-mbt-npm-packages/
  - https://www.stepsecurity.io/blog/mini-shai-hulud-attack-cap-js-mbt-npm-supply-chain-compromise

detection:

    Image|endswith:

    CommandLine|contains: 'setup.mjs'

Mini Shai-Hulud payload file drop: setup.mjs/execution.js by hash & size in node_modules AIInstallation Medium
Hunts the on-disk drop of the two payload files added to the compromised tarballs: setup.mjs (a 4.5KB Bun loader, byte-identical across all four packages) and execution.js (exactly 11,678,349 bytes; SHA256 differs between mbt and @cap-js/*). Matches the six published SHA256 hashes plus name+size+path fallback to cover repackaged variants. Rationale: Combines the six published SHA256 IOCs (high-fidelity exact match) with name+size+path heuristics that survive trivial repackaging: execution.js is documented at exactly 11,678,349 bytes byte-stable across packages, and setup.mjs only legitimately lives in node_modules/mbt or node_modules/@cap-js for this campaign. Cross-validated against Snyk advisory hashes, StepSecurity static deobfuscation, and Socket research. Cross-checked against: • https://snyk.io/blog/bun-based-stealer-hits-sap-cap-js-mbt-npm-packages/ • https://security.snyk.io/package/npm/mbt/1.2.48 • https://www.stepsecurity.io/blog/mini-shai-hulud-attack-cap-js-mbt-npm-supply-chain-compromise • https://socket.dev/blog/mini-shai-hulud-cap-js-mbt-supply-chain
ATT&CKT1195.002 T1027 T1105

Mini Shai-Hulud post-compromise persistence artifacts in .claude/, .vscode/, .github/workflows/ AIActions on Objectives High
Hunts the three novel persistence files committed by the Mini Shai-Hulud payload after it harvests tokens: `.claude/settings.json` (Claude Code SessionStart hook re-execution), `.vscode/tasks.json` (runOn folderOpen), and `.github/workflows/format-check.yml` (typosquatted dependabout branch, dumps `${{ toJSON(secrets) }}` to format-results.txt). Detection fires when these specific paths are written by a non-developer process (node/bun) on a victim machine, OR when a repository checkout introduces them locally. Rationale: Targets the three concrete persistence paths called out by name in the Snyk article and StepSecurity's deobfuscation: `.claude/settings.json` (SessionStart hook — novel AI-agent-config persistence), `.vscode/tasks.json` (runOn folderOpen), and `.github/workflows/format-check.yml` (the typo-branch `dependabout/github_actions/format/setup-formatter` artifact that dumps `${{ toJSON(secrets) }}`). Pairing the path with a node/bun/python/powershell writer process discriminates payload activity from legitimate IDE/editor saves. Cross-validated against Snyk, StepSecurity, the cap-js/cds-dbs#1588 and SAP/cloud-mta-build-tool#1224 GitHub disclosures. Cross-checked against: • https://snyk.io/blog/bun-based-stealer-hits-sap-cap-js-mbt-npm-packages/ • https://www.stepsecurity.io/blog/mini-shai-hulud-attack-cap-js-mbt-npm-supply-chain-compromise • https://github.com/cap-js/cds-dbs/issues/1588 • https://github.com/SAP/cloud-mta-build-tool/issues/1224 • https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1546/
ATT&CKT1546 T1554 T1567
Data sourcesEndpoint.Filesystem
DeviceFileEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(7d)
| where ActionType in ("FileCreated","FileModified","FileRenamed")
| where (FolderPath has @"\.claude\" and FileName =~ "settings.json")
   or (FolderPath has "/.claude/" and FileName =~ "settings.json")
   or (FolderPath has @"\.vscode\" and FileName =~ "tasks.json")
   or (FolderPath has "/.vscode/" and FileName =~ "tasks.json")
   or (FolderPath has @"\.github\workflows" and FileName =~ "format-check.yml")
   or (FolderPath has "/.github/workflows" and FileName =~ "format-check.yml")
| where InitiatingProcessFileName in~ ("node.exe","node","bun.exe","bun","python.exe","python","python3","powershell.exe","pwsh.exe")
| where InitiatingProcessAccountName !endswith "$"
| extend ArtifactKind = case(
      FileName =~ "settings.json" and FolderPath has ".claude", "claude_sessionstart_hook",
      FileName =~ "tasks.json" and FolderPath has ".vscode", "vscode_folderopen_task",
      FileName =~ "format-check.yml", "github_workflow_secret_dump",
      "unknown")
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, ActionType, ArtifactKind, FolderPath, FileName, SHA256,
          Writer = InitiatingProcessFileName,
          WriterCmd = InitiatingProcessCommandLine,
          User = InitiatingProcessAccountName
| order by Timestamp desc
ImFileEvent
| where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
| where EventType in ("FileCreated","FileModified","FileRenamed")
| where (TargetFilePath has "/.claude/" or TargetFilePath has @"\.claude\") and TargetFileName =~ "settings.json"
   or (TargetFilePath has "/.vscode/" or TargetFilePath has @"\.vscode\") and TargetFileName =~ "tasks.json"
   or (TargetFilePath has "/.github/workflows" or TargetFilePath has @"\.github\workflows") and TargetFileName =~ "format-check.yml"
| where ActingProcessName has_any ("node","bun","python","powershell","pwsh")
| where ActorUsername !endswith "$"
| extend ArtifactKind = case(
      TargetFileName =~ "settings.json" and TargetFilePath has ".claude", "claude_sessionstart_hook",
      TargetFileName =~ "tasks.json" and TargetFilePath has ".vscode", "vscode_folderopen_task",
      TargetFileName =~ "format-check.yml", "github_workflow_secret_dump",
      "unknown")
| project TimeGenerated, DvcHostname, EventType, ArtifactKind, TargetFilePath, TargetFileName,
          ActingProcessName, ActingProcessCommandLine, ActorUsername
| order by TimeGenerated desc
title: Mini Shai-Hulud Post-Compromise Persistence Files Written by Node/Bun/Python
id: 9b8e4f31-7d2c-4a6b-91c5-2e8d3f7c9a4b
description: Detects the three persistence artifacts written by the Mini Shai-Hulud payload — .claude/settings.json (SessionStart hook), .vscode/tasks.json (runOn folderOpen), and .github/workflows/format-check.yml (dependabout-typosquat workflow dumping ${{ toJSON(secrets) }} to format-results.txt) — when created by a node, bun, python or powershell process.
references:
  - https://snyk.io/blog/bun-based-stealer-hits-sap-cap-js-mbt-npm-packages/
  - https://www.stepsecurity.io/blog/mini-shai-hulud-attack-cap-js-mbt-npm-supply-chain-compromise
  - https://github.com/cap-js/cds-dbs/issues/1588
  - https://github.com/SAP/cloud-mta-build-tool/issues/1224
author: SOC Detection Engineering
date: 2026/04/29
tags:
  - attack.persistence
  - attack.t1546
  - attack.t1554
logsource:
  category: file_event
  product: windows
detection:
  paths_claude:
    TargetFilename|contains: '\.claude\settings.json'
  paths_vscode:
    TargetFilename|contains: '\.vscode\tasks.json'
  paths_workflow:
    TargetFilename|contains: '\.github\workflows\format-check.yml'
  writer:
    Image|endswith:
      - '\node.exe'
      - '\bun.exe'
      - '\python.exe'
      - '\python3.exe'
      - '\powershell.exe'
      - '\pwsh.exe'

title: Crypto-Wallet Keystore Access by Non-Wallet Process
id: 7c8b2e10-4d4f-4a8c-9c1f-bf6e2c4a8d02
status: experimental
description: |
    Stealers / wallet drainers read keystore files from MetaMask,
    Exodus, Atomic, Phantom, Bitcoin, Electrum, Ethereum-cli wallets.
    Filtering out the legitimate wallet binaries leaves only attacker
    activity.
references:
    - https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1005/
author: Clankerusecase
date: 2026/05/02
tags:
    - attack.t1005
    - attack.collection
logsource:
    category: file_access
    product: windows
detection:
    selection_path:
        TargetFilename|contains:
            - '\Ethereum\keystore\'
            - '\Bitcoin\'
            - '\Exodus\'
            - '\Electrum\wallets\'
            - '\MetaMask\'
            - '\Phantom\'
            - '\Atomic\Local Storage\'
    filter_legit:
        Image|endswith:
            - '\MetaMask.exe'
            - '\Exodus.exe'
            - '\Atomic.exe'
            - '\electrum.exe'
            - '\Bitcoin.exe'
            - '\Phantom.exe'

falsepositives:

level: high

Toggle if your env has no CIM data-model acceleration.

    from datamodel=Endpoint.Filesystem
    where (Filesystem.file_path="*\Ethereum\keystore\*"
        OR Filesystem.file_path="*\Bitcoin\wallet.dat"
        OR Filesystem.file_path="*\Exodus\exodus.wallet*"
        OR Filesystem.file_path="*\Electrum\wallets\*"
        OR Filesystem.file_path="*\MetaMask\*"
        OR Filesystem.file_path="*\Phantom\*"
        OR Filesystem.file_path="*\Atomic\Local Storage\*")
      AND NOT Filesystem.process_name IN ("MetaMask.exe","Exodus.exe","Atomic.exe","electrum.exe","Bitcoin.exe","Phantom.exe")

| `drop_dm_object_name(Filesystem)`

    from datamodel=Endpoint.Filesystem
    where (Filesystem.file_path="*\Ethereum\keystore\*"
        OR Filesystem.file_path="*\Bitcoin\wallet.dat"
        OR Filesystem.file_path="*\Exodus\exodus.wallet*"
        OR Filesystem.file_path="*\Electrum\wallets\*"
        OR Filesystem.file_path="*\MetaMask\*"

title: Infostealer - Non-Browser Process Accessing Browser Credential Stores
id: 7c8b2e10-4d4f-4a8c-9c1f-bf6e2c4a8d01
status: experimental
description: |
    Stealers (RedLine, Lumma, Vidar, Atomic) read Login Data / cookies
    SQLite databases from Chrome/Edge/Firefox profile directories. Any
    non-browser process touching these files is a high-fidelity signal.
references:
    - https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1539/
    - https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1555/003/
author: Clankerusecase
date: 2026/05/02
tags:
    - attack.t1539
    - attack.t1555.003
    - attack.credential-access
logsource:
    category: file_access
    product: windows
detection:
    selection_path:
        TargetFilename|contains:
            - '\Google\Chrome\User Data\'
            - '\Microsoft\Edge\User Data\'
            - '\Mozilla\Firefox\Profiles\'
    selection_file:
        TargetFilename|endswith:
            - '\Login Data'
            - '\Cookies'
            - '\logins.json'
            - '\cookies.sqlite'
    filter_browser:
        Image|endswith:
            - '\chrome.exe'
            - '\msedge.exe'
            - '\firefox.exe'
            - '\brave.exe'
            - '\opera.exe'
    condition: selection_path and selection_file and not filter_browser
falsepositives:
    - Backup utilities reading user profile files
    - Browser sync agents from non-stock vendors
level: high

    where (Filesystem.file_path="*\Google\Chrome\User Data\*\Login Data*"

        OR Filesystem.file_path="*\Microsoft\Edge\User Data\*\Login Data*"
        OR Filesystem.file_path="*\Mozilla\Firefox\Profiles\*\logins.json*"
        OR Filesystem.file_path="*\Mozilla\Firefox\Profiles\*\cookies.sqlite*")
      AND NOT Filesystem.process_name IN ("chrome.exe","msedge.exe","firefox.exe","brave.exe","opera.exe")

| `drop_dm_object_name(Filesystem)`
| tstats summariesonly=false count min(_time) as firstTime max(_time) as lastTime
    from datamodel=Endpoint.Filesystem
    where (Filesystem.file_path="*\Google\Chrome\User Data\*\Login Data*"
        OR Filesystem.file_path="*\Google\Chrome\User Data\*\Cookies*"

        OR Filesystem.file_path="*\Mozilla\Firefox\Profiles\*\logins.json*"

OAuth consent / suspicious app grant Actions on Objectives High
Cloud identity abuse: app gets high-priv scopes, often via consent phishing.
ATT&CKT1528 T1098.001
Data sourcesAuthentication.Authentication CloudAppEvents
CloudAppEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(7d)
| where ActionType in ("Consent to application.","Add OAuth2PermissionGrant.","Add delegated permission grant.")
| project Timestamp, AccountObjectId, AccountDisplayName, ActivityType,
          ActivityObjects, IPAddress, UserAgent
// Entra ID directory audit — user / admin consent to a third-party app.
AuditLogs
| where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
| where OperationName has "Consent to application"
| where Result =~ "success"
| extend AppName = tostring(parse_json(tostring(TargetResources))[0].displayName),
         AppId   = tostring(parse_json(tostring(TargetResources))[0].id),
         User    = tostring(parse_json(tostring(InitiatedBy)).user.userPrincipalName)
| project TimeGenerated, OperationName, User, AppName, AppId, Result
| order by TimeGenerated desc

PowerShell encoded / obfuscated command Exploitation High
Encoded or obfuscated PowerShell — common across loaders, recon, and post-exploitation.
ATT&CKT1059.001 T1027
Data sourcesEndpoint.Processes DeviceProcessEvents
DeviceProcessEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(7d)
| where AccountName !endswith "$"
| where FileName in~ ("powershell.exe","pwsh.exe")
| where ProcessCommandLine matches regex @"(?i)(-enc|encodedcommand|frombase64string|-nop|-w\s+hidden|invoke-expression|iex\s*\(|downloadstring|net\.webclient)"
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, AccountName, ProcessCommandLine,
          InitiatingProcessFileName, InitiatingProcessCommandLine
SecurityEvent
| where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
| where EventID == 4688
| where Account !endswith "$"
| where NewProcessName endswith "\powershell.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\pwsh.exe"
| where CommandLine matches regex @"(?i)(-enc|encodedcommand|frombase64string|-nop|-w\s+hidden|invoke-expression|iex\s*\(|downloadstring|net\.webclient)"
| project TimeGenerated, Computer, Account, NewProcessName,
          CommandLine, ParentProcessName
| order by TimeGenerated desc

title: Obfuscated / Encoded PowerShell Execution
id: 7c8b2e10-4d4f-4a8c-9c1f-bf6e2c4a8d08
status: experimental
description: |
    PowerShell launched with -EncodedCommand, base64 strings, hidden
    window, no-profile, bypass policy, IEX / Invoke-Expression / Net
    .WebClient.DownloadString — combinations indicating evasion.
references:
    - https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1059/001/

author: Clankerusecase

level: high

File hash IOCs — endpoint file/process match Installation High
Match SHA256/SHA1/MD5 named in the article against EDR file/process telemetry.
ATT&CKT1027
Data sourcesEndpoint.Filesystem Endpoint.Processes DeviceFileEvents DeviceProcessEvents
// Pre-filter each table BEFORE the union — the engine cannot push
// predicates across `union`, and DeviceFileEvents lacks ProcessCommandLine
// (Initiating only) so column-projection has to differ per side.
union
    ( DeviceFileEvents
        | where Timestamp > ago(7d)
        | where InitiatingProcessAccountName !endswith "$"
        | where SHA256 in~ ("4066781fa830224c8bbcc3aa005a396657f9c8f9016f9a64ad44a9d7f5f45e34", "80a3d2877813968ef847ae73b5eeeb70b9435254e74d7f07d8cf4057f0a710ac", "6f933d00b7d05678eb43c90963a80b8947c4ae6830182f89df31da9f568fea95", "307d0fa7407d40e67d14e9d5a4c61ac5b4f20431", "0af7415d65753f6aede8c9c0f39be478666b9c12", "4b04304f6d51392e3f43856c94ca95800518a694", "7b6a28e92149637e5d7c7f4a2d3e54acd507c929", "e80824a19f48d778a746571bb15279b5679fd61c", "35baf8316645372eea40b91d48acb067") or SHA1 in~ ("4066781fa830224c8bbcc3aa005a396657f9c8f9016f9a64ad44a9d7f5f45e34", "80a3d2877813968ef847ae73b5eeeb70b9435254e74d7f07d8cf4057f0a710ac", "6f933d00b7d05678eb43c90963a80b8947c4ae6830182f89df31da9f568fea95", "307d0fa7407d40e67d14e9d5a4c61ac5b4f20431", "0af7415d65753f6aede8c9c0f39be478666b9c12", "4b04304f6d51392e3f43856c94ca95800518a694", "7b6a28e92149637e5d7c7f4a2d3e54acd507c929", "e80824a19f48d778a746571bb15279b5679fd61c", "35baf8316645372eea40b91d48acb067") or MD5 in~ ("4066781fa830224c8bbcc3aa005a396657f9c8f9016f9a64ad44a9d7f5f45e34", "80a3d2877813968ef847ae73b5eeeb70b9435254e74d7f07d8cf4057f0a710ac", "6f933d00b7d05678eb43c90963a80b8947c4ae6830182f89df31da9f568fea95", "307d0fa7407d40e67d14e9d5a4c61ac5b4f20431", "0af7415d65753f6aede8c9c0f39be478666b9c12", "4b04304f6d51392e3f43856c94ca95800518a694", "7b6a28e92149637e5d7c7f4a2d3e54acd507c929", "e80824a19f48d778a746571bb15279b5679fd61c", "35baf8316645372eea40b91d48acb067")
        | project Timestamp, DeviceName, ActionType, FileName, FolderPath, SHA256,
                  Cmd = InitiatingProcessCommandLine, Source = "DeviceFileEvents" ),
    ( DeviceProcessEvents

Don't Panic: The Thymeleaf Template Injection That Only Hurts If You Let It (CVE-2026-40478)

Snyk
2026-04-29 4 use cases 1 technique 4 kill-chain phases detected

CVE-2026-40478: The Thymeleaf template injection (CVSS 9.1) is conditional. Patch to 3.1.4+ immediately, and audit your code for dynamic view or template expression misuse, which is the key precondition for exploitability.

CVEsCVE-2026-40478
ATT&CKT1190
Click any ATT&CK pill below to open it on the Matrix
Phase 1
Reconnaissance
Detected
Phase 2
Weaponization
—
Phase 3

—
Phase 4
Exploitation

Detected
Phase 6

Actions on Objectives
Detected
Reconnaissance. Attacker researches the target — OSINT, scanning, enumeration. → Asset exposure — vulnerability matches article CVE(s)
Weaponization. Coupling exploit code with deliverable payload (e.g. weaponized PDF/Office doc, trojanized installer).
Delivery. Transmitting the weapon (phishing email, USB, watering hole, drive-by, malicious ad).
Exploitation. Triggering the exploit — vulnerability/macro/trust abuse to execute code. → [LLM] Thymeleaf SpEL tab-character sandbox bypass payload in HTTP request (CVE-2026-40478)
Installation. Establishing persistence on the host — backdoor, service, scheduled task, registry key. → [LLM] Java/Tomcat process writes .jsp webshell file to disk (CVE-2026-40478 post-exploit drop)
Command & Control. Beacon to attacker infrastructure for control and tasking.
Actions on Objectives. Lateral movement, credential dumping, data theft, ransomware, sabotage. → [LLM] Java/Tomcat process spawns OS command interpreter (post-Thymeleaf SSTI RCE)
Thymeleaf SpEL tab-character sandbox bypass payload in HTTP request (CVE-2026-40478) AIExploitation High
Detects HTTP requests carrying the CVE-2026-40478 Thymeleaf SSTI payload — `new` followed by a tab/`%09` and a Spring Framework class reference (typically `org.springframework.core.io.FileSystemResource` chained to `getOutputStream`). The tab whitespace defeats Thymeleaf's pre-check while SpEL still parses the expression, allowing RCE on apps that pipe user input into the expression engine. Rationale: Anchors on the exact bypass signature called out in the article — the literal `new` keyword + tab (`%09`) + Spring class name, plus the `FileSystemResource(...).getOutputStream()` chain quoted in the PoC. This combination is not produced by benign traffic and pivots on the URL-encoded form most likely to appear in IIS/Nginx access logs. Defender Advanced Hunting has no HTTP request-body table so `defender_kql` is intentionally empty; Falcon FDR does not ship raw HTTP request payloads either.
ATT&CKT1190 T1059
Data sourcesWeb.Web
Expected false positives · estimated rate: medium — model-assessed, tune to your environment
  • Authorized penetration tests running CVE-2026-40478 PoCs against the app
  • Internal vulnerability scanners (Nuclei templates, Tenable, Qualys) emitting the payload during scheduled scans
  • Bug-bounty researchers probing the public Spring Boot endpoint
  • Security training labs / CTF infrastructure deliberately hosting the vulnerable code
  • Java security log shippers that echo back the request URI in error pages, looping the payload into another log line
Suppression filter
// Add to Sentinel query to suppress authorized scanners:
// | where csUserAgent !has_any ("Nuclei", "ZAP", "Burp", "qualys", "tenable", "nessus")
// | where cIP !in ("<authorized-scanner-cidrs>")
Response runbook
Triage: pull the full request (method, URI, body, source IP, user-agent, response code) and check whether the targeted Spring Boot app is on a Thymeleaf version <3.1.4 (or Spring Boot starter <3.5.14 / <4.0.6). A 2xx response is strong evidence of successful injection. Contain: block the source IP at the WAF/edge, pull the host into network quarantine if it accepted the request, and snapshot the Tomcat/Spring Boot process and webapps directory. Hunt: pivot on the same host for any new `.jsp` files written by `java.exe`/`javaw.exe` (UC2) and for Java processes spawning `cmd.exe`/`powershell.exe`/`bash` (UC3) — those confirm RCE rather than just an attempted exploit. Audit the app code for `StringTemplateResolver` + user-controlled input to `templateEngine.process()` as a root-cause fix.
let LookbackDays = 7d;
W3CIISLog
| where TimeGenerated > ago(LookbackDays)
| extend RawRequest = strcat(tostring(csUriStem), "?", tostring(csUriQuery))
| extend DecodedRequest = url_decode(RawRequest)
| where DecodedRequest matches regex @"(?i)new[\t\s]+(?:org\.springframework|java\.lang|java\.io|jakarta\.|javax\.)"
    or RawRequest has_any ("new%09org.springframework", "new%09java.lang", "new%09java.io")
    or (DecodedRequest has "FileSystemResource" and DecodedRequest has "getOutputStream")
| project TimeGenerated, Computer, sSiteName, cIP, csMethod, csUriStem, csUriQuery, DecodedRequest, scStatus, csUserAgent
| order by TimeGenerated desc
title: Thymeleaf SpEL Tab-Character Sandbox Bypass Payload (CVE-2026-40478)
id: 7a3f8d2e-1b4c-4a9e-8f7d-3c2b1a4e5d6f
status: experimental
description: Detects HTTP requests containing the CVE-2026-40478 SSTI payload that abuses a tab character to bypass Thymeleaf's `new` keyword pre-check, then instantiates a Spring FileSystemResource to write a webshell.
references:
  - https://snyk.io/blog/thymeleaf-injection/
author: SOC Detection Engineering
date: 2026/05/21
tags:
  - attack.initial_access
  - attack.t1190
  - attack.execution
  - attack.t1059
logsource:
  category: webserver
detection:
  payload_encoded:
    cs-uri-query|contains:
      - 'new%09org.springframework'
      - 'new%09java.lang'
      - 'new%09java.io'
      - 'new%09jakarta.'
      - 'new%09javax.'
  payload_class_chain:
    cs-uri-query|contains|all:
      - 'FileSystemResource'
      - 'getOutputStream'
  condition: payload_encoded or payload_class_chain
falsepositives:
  - Authorized red-team or bug-bounty scans against the Spring Boot application
  - Vulnerability scanners (Nuclei, Burp, ZAP) emitting templated PoC payloads
level: high

Java/Tomcat process writes .jsp webshell file to disk (CVE-2026-40478 post-exploit drop) AIInstallation High
Detects a Spring Boot / Tomcat / generic Java process creating a `.jsp` or `.jspx` file on disk outside Tomcat's JSP precompilation cache. CVE-2026-40478's PoC uses `new FileSystemResource('shell.jsp').getOutputStream()` to drop a JSP webshell — the file-write event by `java.exe` is a high-fidelity indicator that the SpEL sandbox bypass succeeded. Rationale: The article's PoC explicitly drops `shell.jsp` via `new[TAB]org.springframework.core.io.FileSystemResource('shell.jsp').getOutputStream()`. A JSP write originated by `java.exe`/Tomcat outside the precompilation cache is a textbook web-shell indicator and a direct match for this CVE's impact. Excluding `work\Catalina` and `temp\jsp` removes the dominant FP source (Tomcat's own JSP compiler).
ATT&CKT1505.003 T1190
Data sourcesEndpoint.Filesystem
Expected false positives · estimated rate: low — model-assessed, tune to your environment
  • Custom Tomcat configurations that compile JSPs to a non-standard work directory
  • WAR-file hot-deploy in non-production environments (Maven/Gradle plugins, Spring Boot DevTools)
  • IDE-driven remote deployment from IntelliJ IDEA, Eclipse, NetBeans
  • Application installers / patches that unpack JSPs into `webapps/<app>/` at upgrade time
  • JSP-based templating frameworks (rare) that legitimately generate JSPs at runtime
Suppression filter
// Add to Defender query to suppress build/deploy systems:
// | where InitiatingProcessParentFileName !in~ ("mvn.cmd", "gradle.bat", "jenkins-agent.exe", "TeamCity*.exe")
// | where InitiatingProcessCommandLine !has_any ("DevTools", "-Dspring.devtools", "hot-deploy")
Response runbook
Triage: hash the dropped JSP (SHA256 in the alert), pull its content from the host, and check whether it contains shell-like primitives — `Runtime.getRuntime().exec`, `ProcessBuilder`, `request.getParameter` paired with output streams. Cross-reference the file path with the Tomcat `webapps` deployment directory of the affected Spring Boot app. Contain: stop the Tomcat/Spring Boot service, isolate the host, quarantine the JSP file, and block the source IP from UC1 at the perimeter. Hunt: search the host for child-process events where Java is the parent (UC3), audit the source code for `StringTemplateResolver` misuse, and review the last 30 days of W3CIISLog/ImWebSession for the SpEL payload (UC1) to scope the campaign window. Patch Thymeleaf to 3.1.4+ and the Spring Boot starter to 3.5.14 / 4.0.6.
let LookbackDays = 7d;
DeviceFileEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(LookbackDays)
| where ActionType in ("FileCreated", "FileRenamed", "FileModified")
| where FileName endswith ".jsp" or FileName endswith ".jspx"
| where InitiatingProcessFileName in~ ("java.exe", "javaw.exe", "tomcat.exe", "tomcat9.exe", "tomcat10.exe", "catalina.exe")
   or InitiatingProcessFolderPath has_any ("tomcat", "jboss", "wildfly", "spring-boot", "catalina")
| where not(FolderPath has_any (@"\work\Catalina\", @"\temp\jsp\", "/work/Catalina/", "/temp/jsp/"))
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, FileName, FolderPath, SHA256,
          InitiatingProcessFileName, InitiatingProcessFolderPath,
          InitiatingProcessCommandLine, InitiatingProcessAccountName,
          InitiatingProcessParentFileName
| order by Timestamp desc
let LookbackDays = 7d;
ImFileEvent
| where TimeGenerated > ago(LookbackDays)
| where EventType == "FileCreated"
| where TargetFileExtension in~ ("jsp", "jspx")
| where ActingProcessName has_any ("java.exe", "javaw.exe", "tomcat", "catalina")
   or ActingProcessCommandLine has_any ("spring-boot", "catalina", "-jar")
| where not(TargetFilePath has_any (@"\work\Catalina\", "/work/Catalina/", @"\temp\jsp\", "/temp/jsp/"))
| project TimeGenerated, DvcHostname, TargetFilePath, TargetFileName, TargetFileSHA256,
          ActingProcessName, ActingProcessCommandLine, ActorUsername
| order by TimeGenerated desc

Java/Tomcat process spawns OS command interpreter (post-Thymeleaf SSTI RCE) AIActions on Objectives Medium
Detects a Java application-server process (java.exe, javaw.exe, Tomcat) spawning a Windows or Unix command shell — the RCE stage of CVE-2026-40478, where the dropped JSP webshell calls ProcessBuilder to execute arbitrary OS commands. Filters out service-account installations of Java itself to keep signal high. Rationale: The article states the exploit drops a JSP that calls `ProcessBuilder` to execute the RCE — i.e. java.exe (the Tomcat/Spring Boot process) becomes the parent of an OS shell or reconnaissance binary. This parent-child pair is rare in production Java workloads outside CI/CD agents and monitoring tools. The query mirrors the BluRaven `pattern-process-tree` house style — parent narrows scope, child narrows behaviour.
ATT&CKT1059.003 T1059.001 T1059.004 T1190
Data sourcesEndpoint.Processes
Expected false positives · estimated rate: medium — model-assessed, tune to your environment
  • Jenkins / TeamCity / GitLab Runner Java-based build agents that legitimately spawn `cmd`/`powershell` build steps
  • Spring Boot Actuator endpoints or custom health-checks shelling out for `ipconfig` / `systeminfo` / `hostname` results
  • APM agents (Dynatrace, AppDynamics, New Relic Java) invoking native diagnostics
  • JNI-based integrations that wrap OS utilities (e.g. legacy Java apps invoking `net.exe` for user lookups)
  • Tomcat startup scripts that briefly invoke `whoami.exe` / `hostname.exe` during initialization
Suppression filter
// Add to Defender query to suppress known CI/CD agents and monitoring:
// | where InitiatingProcessParentFileName !in~ ("jenkins-agent.exe", "TeamCity*.exe", "runner.exe", "gitlab-runner.exe")
// | where InitiatingProcessCommandLine !has_any ("jenkins", "-Dteamcity", "gitlab-runner", "dynatrace", "appdynamics", "newrelic")
// | where not (FileName =~ "hostname.exe" and InitiatingProcessCommandLine has "catalina.sh start")
Response runbook
Triage: capture the full process tree (grandparent → java.exe → child) and the child's command line. A child invoking `whoami` / `net user` / `ipconfig` / `systeminfo` within seconds of one another is reconnaissance and far more suspicious than a single isolated `cmd.exe`. Cross-reference the host with UC2 — if a fresh JSP was dropped in the same hour, treat as confirmed exploitation. Contain: stop the Tomcat/Spring Boot service, isolate the host at the network layer, preserve memory for triage, and rotate any service-account credentials the JVM had access to (keystores, application.yml secrets, cloud IAM tokens on the host). Hunt: query the last 30 days for the same parent-child pattern on every Java application-server host; look for outbound network connections initiated by `java.exe` to non-corporate destinations (potential C2). Patch Thymeleaf to 3.1.4+ and fix the underlying `StringTemplateResolver` misuse identified in the code review.
let LookbackDays = 7d;
DeviceProcessEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(LookbackDays)
| where InitiatingProcessFileName in~ ("java.exe", "javaw.exe", "tomcat.exe", "tomcat9.exe", "tomcat10.exe", "catalina.exe")
   or InitiatingProcessFolderPath has_any ("tomcat", "catalina", "spring-boot")
| where FileName in~ ("cmd.exe", "powershell.exe", "pwsh.exe", "wscript.exe", "cscript.exe", "bash.exe", "sh.exe", "whoami.exe", "net.exe", "net1.exe", "ipconfig.exe", "systeminfo.exe", "wmic.exe", "certutil.exe", "bitsadmin.exe", "curl.exe", "wget.exe", "tasklist.exe", "hostname.exe")
| where AccountName !endswith "$"
| where InitiatingProcessParentFileName !in~ ("services.exe")
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, AccountName,
          ParentImage = InitiatingProcessFolderPath,
          ParentCmd   = InitiatingProcessCommandLine,
          ChildImage  = FolderPath,
          ChildCmd    = ProcessCommandLine,
          SHA256
| order by Timestamp desc
let LookbackDays = 7d;
ImProcessCreate
| where TimeGenerated > ago(LookbackDays)
| where ActingProcessName has_any ("java.exe", "javaw.exe", "tomcat", "catalina")
   or ActingProcessCommandLine has_any ("spring-boot", "catalina", "-Dcatalina")
| where TargetProcessName has_any ("cmd.exe", "powershell.exe", "pwsh.exe", "wscript.exe", "cscript.exe", "bash", "/bin/sh", "whoami", "net.exe", "ipconfig", "systeminfo", "wmic.exe", "certutil.exe", "bitsadmin.exe", "curl", "wget", "tasklist", "hostname")
| where ActorUsername !endswith "$"
| project TimeGenerated, DvcHostname, ActorUsername,
          ParentName = ActingProcessName, ParentCmd = ActingProcessCommandLine,
          ChildName  = TargetProcessName, ChildCmd  = TargetProcessCommandLine,
          Hash
| order by TimeGenerated desc

Attackers exploited a GitHub Actions script injection vulnerability to publish a malicious version of the elementary-data Python CLI (v0.23.3), embedding a credential-stealing backdoor that targeted dbt profiles, cloud provider keys, and SSH secrets from data engineering environments.

Reconnaissance. Attacker researches the target — OSINT, scanning, enumeration.
Weaponization. Coupling exploit code with deliverable payload (e.g. weaponized PDF/Office doc, trojanized installer).
Delivery. Transmitting the weapon (phishing email, USB, watering hole, drive-by, malicious ad). → [LLM] Compromised elementary-data==0.23.3 PyPI install on developer / CI host
Exploitation. Triggering the exploit — vulnerability/macro/trust abuse to execute code. → PowerShell encoded / obfuscated command · Trusted vendor binary / installer launching unusual children · Article-specific behavioural hunt — Malicious Release of elementary-data PyPI Package Steals Cloud Credentials from
Installation. Establishing persistence on the host — backdoor, service, scheduled task, registry key. → [LLM] Trinny marker file creation (.trinny-security-update) · File hash IOCs — endpoint file/process match
Command & Control. Beacon to attacker infrastructure for control and tasking. → [LLM] Exfil to skyhanni.cloud C2 with X-Rise-To-The-Trinny header · Beaconing — periodic outbound to small set of destinations · Network connections to article IPs / domains
Actions on Objectives. Lateral movement, credential dumping, data theft, ransomware, sabotage. → [LLM] Credential archive staging — trin.tar.gz created by python process · OAuth consent / suspicious app grant
Compromised elementary-data==0.23.3 PyPI install on developer / CI host AIDelivery High
Detects pip / pipx / uv installing the known-malicious elementary-data 0.23.3 release pushed by TeamPCP via the GitHub Actions script-injection on April 24-26 2026. Catches both interactive `pip install elementary-data==0.23.3` and lockfile-pinned reinstalls on CI runners. Fires on the install command itself before the credential-stealing .pth payload executes. Rationale: Anchored on the exact compromised package coordinates `elementary-data==0.23.3` from the Snyk advisory SNYK-PYTHON-ELEMENTARYDATA-16316110, plus the standard Python installer process names. Cross-checked against StepSecurity and Trend Micro write-ups which confirm the same version string as the sole malicious release. Cross-checked against: • https://www.stepsecurity.io/blog/elementary-data-compromised-on-pypi-and-ghcr-forged-release-pushed-via-github-actions-script-injection • https://www.trendmicro.com/en_us/research/26/e/analyzing-teampcp-supply-chain-attacks.html • https://www.chainguard.dev/unchained/chainguard-customers-safe-from-elementary-data-compromise • https://securitylabs.datadoghq.com/articles/litellm-compromised-pypi-teampcp-supply-chain-campaign/
ATT&CKT1195.002 T1059.006
Data sourcesEndpoint.Processes
Expected false positives · estimated rate: low — model-assessed, tune to your environment
  • Security researcher reproducing the IOC in an isolated sandbox VM
  • SBOM / dependency-scanner enumerating known-bad versions in a controlled scan
  • Internal incident-response playbook validation that intentionally installs 0.23.3 in a contained lab
  • Stale lockfile (requirements.txt / poetry.lock) on a CI runner that has not been refreshed to 0.23.4
Suppression filter
| where InitiatingProcessFileName !in~ ("trivy.exe","trivy","grype","grype.exe","snyk.exe","snyk","safety","safety.exe","pip-audit","pip-audit.exe")
| where InitiatingProcessCommandLine !has "--dry-run"
Response runbook
1) Triage: identify whether the install completed on a developer workstation, CI runner, or production host. Pull site-packages/elementary.pth — if it contains base64-then-XOR obfuscated Python with the `swabag` keystream seed, you have positive execution. Check `$TMPDIR/.trinny-security-update` or `%TEMP%\.trinny-security-update` for the marker file. 2) Contain: isolate the host, rotate every credential reachable from it — dbt profiles.yml, Snowflake/BigQuery/Redshift, AWS/GCP/Azure keys, IMDS role bindings, GitHub PATs, SSH keys, .npmrc/.pypirc, Kubernetes ServiceAccount tokens, .env files. For CI runners, revoke the runner's GITHUB_TOKEN scope and rotate any OIDC-bound cloud roles. 3) Hunt: pivot to UC2/UC3/UC4 to find post-install execution, trin.tar.gz staging, and exfil to skyhanni.cloud. Search lockfiles across the org for any remaining 0.23.3 pin.
DeviceProcessEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(30d)
| where ProcessCommandLine has "elementary-data"
| where ProcessCommandLine has "0.23.3"
| where ProcessCommandLine has_any ("pip install", "pip3 install", "pip download", "uv pip", "pipx install", "poetry add", "poetry install")
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, AccountName, FileName, ProcessCommandLine, InitiatingProcessFileName, InitiatingProcessCommandLine, InitiatingProcessParentFileName
| order by Timestamp desc
union isfuzzy=true
(SecurityEvent
  | where TimeGenerated > ago(30d)
  | where EventID == 4688
  | where CommandLine has "elementary-data" and CommandLine has "0.23.3"
  | where CommandLine has_any ("pip install", "pip3 install", "uv pip", "pipx install", "poetry")
  | project TimeGenerated, Computer, Account=SubjectUserName, NewProcessName, CommandLine, ParentProcessName),
(ImProcessCreate
  | where TimeGenerated > ago(30d)
  | where ActingProcessCommandLine has "elementary-data" and ActingProcessCommandLine has "0.23.3"
  | where ActingProcessCommandLine has_any ("pip install", "pip3 install", "uv pip", "pipx install", "poetry")
  | project TimeGenerated, DvcHostname, ActorUsername, ActingProcessName, ActingProcessCommandLine, ParentProcessName),
(Syslog
  | where TimeGenerated > ago(30d)
  | where SyslogMessage has "elementary-data" and SyslogMessage has "0.23.3"
  | where SyslogMessage has_any ("pip install", "pip3 install", "uv pip", "pipx install")
  | project TimeGenerated, Computer, ProcessName, SyslogMessage)
| order by TimeGenerated desc
title: Install of Compromised elementary-data 0.23.3 (TeamPCP Supply Chain)
id: 8e3c1b4a-7a2f-4e44-9a5c-12d4a7e9c001
status: experimental
description: Detects pip / uv / pipx / poetry installing the malicious elementary-data 0.23.3 release published by TeamPCP via GitHub Actions script injection in April 2026.
references:
  - https://snyk.io/blog/malicious-release-of-elementary-data-pypi-package-steals-cloud-credentials-from-data-engineers/
  - https://www.stepsecurity.io/blog/elementary-data-compromised-on-pypi-and-ghcr-forged-release-pushed-via-github-actions-script-injection
  - https://www.trendmicro.com/en_us/research/26/e/analyzing-teampcp-supply-chain-attacks.html
author: SOC Detection Engineering
date: 2026/05/21
tags:
  - attack.initial_access
  - attack.t1195.002
  - attack.t1059.006
logsource:
  category: process_creation
detection:
  selection_installer:
    CommandLine|contains:
      - 'pip install'
      - 'pip3 install'
      - 'pip download'
      - 'uv pip install'
      - 'pipx install'
      - 'poetry add'
      - 'poetry install'
  selection_target:
    CommandLine|contains: 'elementary-data'
  selection_version:
    CommandLine|contains: '0.23.3'
  condition: all of selection_*
falsepositives:
  - Pinned reinstall by an engineer who has not yet upgraded to 0.23.4 (still requires remediation)
level: high
(source:windows.sysmon @EventID:1) OR (source:windows.security @EventID:4688) OR (source:linux.auditd @auditd.type:EXECVE) @CommandLine:(*elementary-data*0.23.3* OR *elementary\-data*0.23.3*)
#event_simpleName=ProcessRollup2
| CommandLine=/elementary[-_]data/i
| CommandLine=/0\.23\.3/
| CommandLine=/(pip|pip3|uv pip|pipx|poetry (add|install))/i
| groupBy([aid, ComputerName, UserName, ImageFileName, CommandLine], function=count())
ENDPOINT
Toggle if your env has no CIM data-model acceleration.
| tstats summariesonly=true count min(_time) as firstTime max(_time) as lastTime values(Processes.process) as process values(Processes.parent_process) as parent_process from datamodel=Endpoint.Processes where (Processes.process_name IN ("pip.exe","pip3.exe","pip","pip3","python.exe","python","python3","uv.exe","uv","pipx","pipx.exe") OR Processes.process="*pip install*" OR Processes.process="*pip3 install*" OR Processes.process="*uv pip install*" OR Processes.process="*pipx install*") Processes.process="*elementary-data*" Processes.process="*0.23.3*" by Processes.dest Processes.user Processes.process_name | `drop_dm_object_name(Processes)` | convert ctime(firstTime) ctime(lastTime)
| tstats summariesonly=false count min(_time) as firstTime max(_time) as lastTime values(Processes.process) as process values(Processes.parent_process) as parent_process from datamodel=Endpoint.Processes where (Processes.process_name IN ("pip.exe","pip3.exe","pip","pip3","python.exe","python","python3","uv.exe","uv","pipx","pipx.exe") OR Processes.process="*pip install*" OR Processes.process="*pip3 install*" OR Processes.process="*uv pip install*" OR Processes.process="*pipx install*") Processes.process="*elementary-data*" Processes.process="*0.23.3*" by Processes.dest Processes.user Processes.process_name | `drop_dm_object_name(Processes)` | convert ctime(firstTime) ctime(lastTime)
Trinny marker file creation (.trinny-security-update) AIInstallation High
Detects the TeamPCP elementary-data malware writing its execution-success marker file `.trinny-security-update` under the system temp directory ($TMPDIR on Linux/macOS, %TEMP% on Windows). This is the most reliable post-execution proof that the malicious .pth payload ran on a host. Rationale: The article explicitly names `$TMPDIR/.trinny-security-update` and `%TEMP%\.trinny-security-update` as the malware's execution marker. The filename is sufficiently unique (no legitimate software uses it) that a single match is high-confidence. Corroborated by StepSecurity and Trend Micro write-ups of the same IOC. Cross-checked against: • https://www.stepsecurity.io/blog/elementary-data-compromised-on-pypi-and-ghcr-forged-release-pushed-via-github-actions-script-injection • https://www.trendmicro.com/en_us/research/26/e/analyzing-teampcp-supply-chain-attacks.html
ATT&CKT1070.004 T1059.006
Data sourcesEndpoint.Filesystem
Expected false positives · estimated rate: low — model-assessed, tune to your environment
  • IR team intentionally re-detonating the sample in a contained lab
  • Forensic image of an already-compromised host being re-scanned by a new EDR agent
  • Threat-emulation tooling (Atomic Red Team / similar) replaying the IOC for control validation
  • Backup software restoring a previously-infected /tmp tree to a clean host
Response runbook
1) Triage: pull the writing process from InitiatingProcessFileName/ContextImageFileName — almost always python.exe/python3 spawned by pip during install, or python at interpreter startup post-install (because .pth runs on every python launch). Confirm presence of elementary.pth in the active venv's site-packages. 2) Contain: kill any running python on the host, isolate from network, revoke and rotate every credential listed in UC1 step 2 (especially IMDS-bound IAM roles if this is an EC2/GCE/AKS node). Treat the host as fully credentialed-compromised. 3) Hunt: search 24h either side for outbound DNS to skyhanni.cloud (UC4) and creation of trin.tar.gz (UC3). Search for other recently-installed PyPI packages with .pth files (LiteLLM v1.82.8 used the same technique).
DeviceFileEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(30d)
| where FileName =~ ".trinny-security-update"
| where ActionType in ("FileCreated","FileModified","FileRenamed")
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, ActionType, FolderPath, FileName, InitiatingProcessFileName, InitiatingProcessCommandLine, InitiatingProcessAccountName, InitiatingProcessParentFileName
| order by Timestamp desc
union isfuzzy=true
(ImFileEvent
  | where TimeGenerated > ago(30d)
  | where TargetFileName =~ ".trinny-security-update" or TargetFilePath endswith ".trinny-security-update"
  | project TimeGenerated, DvcHostname, ActorUsername, ActingProcessName, ActingProcessCommandLine, TargetFilePath, TargetFileName),
(Syslog
  | where TimeGenerated > ago(30d)
  | where SyslogMessage has ".trinny-security-update"
  | project TimeGenerated, Computer, ProcessName, SyslogMessage)
| order by TimeGenerated desc
title: TeamPCP elementary-data Trinny Marker File Created
id: 2c91d77b-3f1e-4d3a-9b22-5e7f8c1a0c02
status: experimental
description: Detects creation of the `.trinny-security-update` marker file dropped under temp by the malicious elementary-data 0.23.3 PyPI package. The file is the malware's execution success indicator.
references:
  - https://snyk.io/blog/malicious-release-of-elementary-data-pypi-package-steals-cloud-credentials-from-data-engineers/
  - https://www.stepsecurity.io/blog/elementary-data-compromised-on-pypi-and-ghcr-forged-release-pushed-via-github-actions-script-injection
author: SOC Detection Engineering
date: 2026/05/21
tags:

  - attack.t1059.006
logsource:
  category: file_event
detection:
  selection:
    TargetFilename|endswith: '\.trinny-security-update'
  condition: selection
falsepositives:
  - None expected; filename is malware-unique
level: critical
(source:windows.sysmon @EventID:11 @TargetFilename:(*\\.trinny-security-update OR *\\.Trinny-Security-Update)) OR (source:linux.auditd @auditd.type:PATH @file.path:*/.trinny-security-update)
#event_simpleName=FileWritten
| TargetFileName=/\.trinny-security-update$/i
| groupBy([aid, ComputerName, UserName, ContextImageFileName, TargetFileName], function=count())
ENDPOINT
Toggle if your env has no CIM data-model acceleration.
| tstats summariesonly=true count min(_time) as firstTime max(_time) as lastTime values(Filesystem.file_path) as file_path values(Filesystem.process_name) as process_name from datamodel=Endpoint.Filesystem where Filesystem.file_name=".trinny-security-update" by Filesystem.dest Filesystem.user Filesystem.action | `drop_dm_object_name(Filesystem)` | convert ctime(firstTime) ctime(lastTime)
| tstats summariesonly=false count min(_time) as firstTime max(_time) as lastTime values(Filesystem.file_path) as file_path values(Filesystem.process_name) as process_name from datamodel=Endpoint.Filesystem where Filesystem.file_name=".trinny-security-update" by Filesystem.dest Filesystem.user Filesystem.action | `drop_dm_object_name(Filesystem)` | convert ctime(firstTime) ctime(lastTime)
Credential archive staging — trin.tar.gz created by python process AIActions on Objectives High
Detects the elementary-data malware's collection stage: it tars every harvested credential file (dbt profiles, AWS/GCP/Azure creds, SSH keys, .kube/config, .env files, crypto wallets) into a file named `trin.tar.gz` immediately before exfil via curl --data-binary. Catches the staging step even if the exfil HTTP connection is later blocked. Rationale: The article explicitly states the malware `Packed all collected material into an archive named trin.tar.gz`. The filename is malware-unique and ties directly to the collection step — corroborated across Snyk, StepSecurity, and Trend Micro reporting on the same TeamPCP campaign. Cross-checked against: • https://www.stepsecurity.io/blog/elementary-data-compromised-on-pypi-and-ghcr-forged-release-pushed-via-github-actions-script-injection • https://www.trendmicro.com/en_us/research/26/e/analyzing-teampcp-supply-chain-attacks.html
ATT&CKT1560.001 T1552.001
Data sourcesEndpoint.Filesystem
Expected false positives · estimated rate: low — model-assessed, tune to your environment
  • Threat-emulation tooling replaying the IOC during purple-team exercise
  • DFIR team reproducing the payload in a contained sandbox
  • Backup/restore tooling cloning a previously-infected /tmp tree
  • A user manually saving a tarball coincidentally named trin.tar.gz (vanishingly unlikely)
Response runbook
1) Triage: confirm the writing process is python / curl / tar spawned from an unprivileged user context, capture the file before it is wiped post-exfil. Hash and submit to TI for confirmation. 2) Contain: isolate host immediately, kill all python and curl processes, block egress to *.skyhanni.cloud at the firewall. Treat every credential that was on the box as compromised — rotate dbt profiles, all cloud provider keys, all SSH keys, IMDS-attached IAM roles, Kubernetes ServiceAccount tokens, .npmrc/.pypirc, .vault-token, .netrc, .pgpass, .my.cnf, every .env in /repos. 3) Hunt: pivot to UC4 to confirm exfiltration completed or was blocked. Search org-wide for other hosts with the same archive name or .trinny-security-update marker (UC2). Audit GitHub Actions workflows for the same script-injection class flaw (interpolating `github.event.comment.body` into a `run:` block).
DeviceFileEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(30d)
| where FileName =~ "trin.tar.gz"
| where ActionType in ("FileCreated","FileModified","FileRenamed")
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, ActionType, FolderPath, FileName, FileSize, InitiatingProcessFileName, InitiatingProcessCommandLine, InitiatingProcessAccountName
| order by Timestamp desc
union isfuzzy=true
(ImFileEvent
  | where TimeGenerated > ago(30d)
  | where TargetFileName =~ "trin.tar.gz"
  | project TimeGenerated, DvcHostname, ActorUsername, ActingProcessName, ActingProcessCommandLine, TargetFilePath, TargetFileName, TargetFileSize),
(Syslog
  | where TimeGenerated > ago(30d)
  | where SyslogMessage has "trin.tar.gz"
  | project TimeGenerated, Computer, ProcessName, SyslogMessage)
| order by TimeGenerated desc
title: TeamPCP elementary-data Credential Archive Staged (trin.tar.gz)
id: 4a6e2f15-d8c3-4b9f-8a11-cb74e205a0c3
status: experimental
description: Detects creation of the `trin.tar.gz` archive used by the malicious elementary-data 0.23.3 PyPI package to bundle harvested cloud credentials and SSH keys prior to exfiltration.
references:
  - https://snyk.io/blog/malicious-release-of-elementary-data-pypi-package-steals-cloud-credentials-from-data-engineers/
  - https://www.stepsecurity.io/blog/elementary-data-compromised-on-pypi-and-ghcr-forged-release-pushed-via-github-actions-script-injection
author: SOC Detection Engineering
date: 2026/05/21
tags:
  - attack.collection
  - attack.t1560.001
  - attack.t1552.001
logsource:
  category: file_event
detection:
  selection:
    TargetFilename|endswith: '\trin.tar.gz'
  condition: selection
falsepositives:
  - Extremely unlikely; filename is malware-unique and not produced by any known legitimate tool
level: critical
(source:windows.sysmon @EventID:11 @TargetFilename:(*\\trin.tar.gz OR *\\Trin.tar.gz)) OR (source:linux.auditd @auditd.type:PATH @file.path:(*/trin.tar.gz OR */Trin.tar.gz))
#event_simpleName=FileWritten
| TargetFileName=/(^|[\\/])trin\.tar\.gz$/i
| groupBy([aid, ComputerName, UserName, ContextImageFileName, TargetFileName, WrittenBytes], function=count())
CLOUD
Toggle if your env has no CIM data-model acceleration.
| tstats summariesonly=true count min(_time) as firstTime max(_time) as lastTime values(Filesystem.file_path) as file_path values(Filesystem.process_name) as process_name from datamodel=Endpoint.Filesystem where Filesystem.file_name="trin.tar.gz" by Filesystem.dest Filesystem.user Filesystem.action | `drop_dm_object_name(Filesystem)` | convert ctime(firstTime) ctime(lastTime)
| tstats summariesonly=false count min(_time) as firstTime max(_time) as lastTime values(Filesystem.file_path) as file_path values(Filesystem.process_name) as process_name from datamodel=Endpoint.Filesystem where Filesystem.file_name="trin.tar.gz" by Filesystem.dest Filesystem.user Filesystem.action | `drop_dm_object_name(Filesystem)` | convert ctime(firstTime) ctime(lastTime)
Exfil to skyhanni.cloud C2 with X-Rise-To-The-Trinny header AICommand & Control High
Detects the TeamPCP elementary-data malware exfiltrating the trin.tar.gz credential archive to the campaign C2 at igotnofriendsonlineorirl-imgonnakmslmao.skyhanni.cloud, identified by either DNS/network egress to the FQDN or the curl command line carrying the bespoke `X-Rise-To-The-Trinny: agree` HTTP header. Rationale: Anchored on three malware-unique strings from the article: the full C2 FQDN `igotnofriendsonlineorirl-imgonnakmslmao.skyhanni.cloud`, the bespoke HTTP header `X-Rise-To-The-Trinny: agree`, and the exfil filename `trin.tar.gz` with `curl --data-binary`. The header and FQDN are sufficiently unique that any single match is high-confidence; corroborated by Snyk, StepSecurity, Trend Micro, and Datadog Security Labs reporting on the same TeamPCP campaign infrastructure. Cross-checked against: • https://www.stepsecurity.io/blog/elementary-data-compromised-on-pypi-and-ghcr-forged-release-pushed-via-github-actions-script-injection • https://www.trendmicro.com/en_us/research/26/e/analyzing-teampcp-supply-chain-attacks.html • https://securitylabs.datadoghq.com/articles/litellm-compromised-pypi-teampcp-supply-chain-campaign/
ATT&CKT1041 T1071.001 T1567
Data sourcesNetwork_Traffic.All_Traffic Network_Resolution.DNS Endpoint.Processes
Expected false positives · estimated rate: low — model-assessed, tune to your environment
  • Threat-intel analyst manually browsing the IOC for analysis (browser User-Agent, not curl)
  • SOC sandbox detonating the sample in a contained environment
  • TI vendor enrichment lookups against the FQDN from a designated research host
  • Note: the parent `skyhanni.cloud` domain hosts unrelated content (Minecraft mod CDN); a wildcard on `*.skyhanni.cloud` alone is not enough — pair with the FQDN, the curl context, or the X-Rise-To-The-Trinny header to keep precision high
Suppression filter
| where InitiatingProcessFileName !in~ ("chrome.exe","msedge.exe","firefox.exe","brave.exe","safari","thor.exe") or ProcessCommandLine has_any ("X-Rise-To-The-Trinny","trin.tar.gz","--data-binary")
Response runbook
1) Triage: confirm whether the connection succeeded or was blocked (RemoteIPType, NetworkConnectIP4 result, firewall accept/deny). If the curl process command line carries `X-Rise-To-The-Trinny: agree` and `--data-binary @trin.tar.gz`, treat as confirmed exfil. Capture pcap if available — the article notes the body is the raw tarball, so the wire data IS the stolen credential bundle. 2) Contain: block `*.skyhanni.cloud` (and specifically `igotnofriendsonlineorirl-imgonnakmslmao.skyhanni.cloud`) at perimeter + DNS RPZ. Isolate host. Rotate every credential listed in UC1 step 2 immediately — assume full exfil. For CI runners: invalidate the runner's GITHUB_TOKEN session, rotate the OIDC trust on any cloud roles the runner could assume, and audit the last 7 days of pushes/tags/releases from that runner identity for anything resembling the malicious commit `b1e4b1f3aad0d489ab0e9208031c67402bbb8480` orphan-commit pattern. 3) Hunt: search 30 days back across the whole estate for the same FQD
let Egress = DeviceNetworkEvents
  | where Timestamp > ago(30d)
  | where RemoteUrl has "skyhanni.cloud" or RemoteUrl has "igotnofriendsonlineorirl-imgonnakmslmao"
  | project Timestamp, DeviceName, RemoteUrl, RemoteIP, RemotePort, InitiatingProcessFileName, InitiatingProcessCommandLine, InitiatingProcessAccountName;
let Curl = DeviceProcessEvents
  | where Timestamp > ago(30d)
  | where ProcessCommandLine has_any ("X-Rise-To-The-Trinny", "igotnofriendsonlineorirl-imgonnakmslmao", "skyhanni.cloud")
     or (FileName in~ ("curl.exe","curl","wget.exe","wget") and ProcessCommandLine has "trin.tar.gz" and ProcessCommandLine has "--data-binary")
  | project Timestamp, DeviceName, AccountName, FileName, ProcessCommandLine, InitiatingProcessFileName, InitiatingProcessCommandLine;
union Egress, Curl
| order by Timestamp desc
union isfuzzy=true
(DnsEvents
  | where TimeGenerated > ago(30d)
  | where Name has "skyhanni.cloud" or Name has "igotnofriendsonlineorirl-imgonnakmslmao"
  | project TimeGenerated, Computer, ClientIP, Name, QueryType, ResultCode),
(CommonSecurityLog
  | where TimeGenerated > ago(30d)
  | where DestinationHostName has "skyhanni.cloud" or RequestURL has "skyhanni.cloud" or RequestURL has "igotnofriendsonlineorirl-imgonnakmslmao"
  | project TimeGenerated, SourceIP, DestinationIP, DestinationHostName, RequestURL, RequestClientApplication, DeviceVendor, DeviceProduct),
(ImWebSession
  | where TimeGenerated > ago(30d)
  | where HttpHostName has "skyhanni.cloud" or Url has "skyhanni.cloud" or Url has "igotnofriendsonlineorirl-imgonnakmslmao"
  | project TimeGenerated, SrcIpAddr, SrcHostname, SrcUsername, Url, HttpHostName, HttpMethod, HttpRequestHeaderUserAgent),
(SecurityEvent
  | where TimeGenerated > ago(30d)
  | where EventID == 4688
  | where CommandLine has_any ("X-Rise-To-The-Trinny", "igotnofriendsonlineorirl-imgonnakmslmao", "skyhanni.cloud")
     or (NewProcessName endswith "\\curl.exe" and CommandLine has "trin.tar.gz" and CommandLine has "--data-binary")
  | project TimeGenerated, Computer, Account=SubjectUserName, NewProcessName, CommandLine, ParentProcessName)
| order by TimeGenerated desc
title: TeamPCP elementary-data C2 Egress to skyhanni.cloud
id: 9d4f1a82-2e6b-4c7a-bc15-3a8f9d6e0c04
status: experimental
description: Detects DNS or HTTP egress to the TeamPCP elementary-data campaign C2 domain `igotnofriendsonlineorirl-imgonnakmslmao.skyhanni.cloud` used to receive the trin.tar.gz credential archive.
references:
  - https://snyk.io/blog/malicious-release-of-elementary-data-pypi-package-steals-cloud-credentials-from-data-engineers/
  - https://www.stepsecurity.io/blog/elementary-data-compromised-on-pypi-and-ghcr-forged-release-pushed-via-github-actions-script-injection
  - https://securitylabs.datadoghq.com/articles/litellm-compromised-pypi-teampcp-supply-chain-campaign/
author: SOC Detection Engineering
date: 2026/05/21
tags:
  - attack.exfiltration
  - attack.command_and_control
  - attack.t1041
  - attack.t1071.001
  - attack.t1567
logsource:
  category: dns
detection:
  selection:
    query|contains:
      - 'skyhanni.cloud'
      - 'igotnofriendsonlineorirl-imgonnakmslmao'
  condition: selection
falsepositives:
  - Threat-intel sandbox replaying the IOC
level: critical
(source:windows.sysmon @EventID:3 @DestinationHostname:(*skyhanni.cloud OR igotnofriendsonlineorirl-imgonnakmslmao.skyhanni.cloud)) OR (source:windows.sysmon @EventID:1 @CommandLine:(*X-Rise-To-The-Trinny* OR *igotnofriendsonlineorirl-imgonnakmslmao* OR *skyhanni.cloud*)) OR (source:windows.security @EventID:4688 @CommandLine:(*X-Rise-To-The-Trinny* OR *skyhanni.cloud*)) OR (source:linux.auditd @auditd.type:EXECVE @process.command_line:(*X-Rise-To-The-Trinny* OR *skyhanni.cloud* OR *igotnofriendsonlineorirl-imgonnakmslmao*))
(#event_simpleName=DnsRequest DomainName=/(^|\.)skyhanni\.cloud$/i)
OR (#event_simpleName=NetworkConnectIP4 ContextImageFileName=/(curl|wget|python|python3|pip|pip3)/i)
OR (#event_simpleName=ProcessRollup2 CommandLine=/(X-Rise-To-The-Trinny|igotnofriendsonlineorirl-imgonnakmslmao|skyhanni\.cloud)/i)
OR (#event_simpleName=ProcessRollup2 ImageFileName=/(curl|wget)(\.exe)?$/i CommandLine=/trin\.tar\.gz/i CommandLine=/--data-binary/i)
| groupBy([aid, ComputerName, UserName, ContextImageFileName, ImageFileName, DomainName, CommandLine], function=count())
NETWORK
Toggle if your env has no CIM data-model acceleration.
| tstats summariesonly=true count min(_time) as firstTime max(_time) as lastTime values(All_Traffic.src) as src values(All_Traffic.dest) as dest from datamodel=Network_Traffic.All_Traffic where (All_Traffic.dest="*skyhanni.cloud" OR All_Traffic.dest_host="*skyhanni.cloud" OR All_Traffic.url="*skyhanni.cloud*" OR All_Traffic.dest_host="igotnofriendsonlineorirl-imgonnakmslmao.skyhanni.cloud") by All_Traffic.dest_host All_Traffic.app All_Traffic.user | `drop_dm_object_name(All_Traffic)` | append [| tstats summariesonly=true count from datamodel=Endpoint.Processes where (Processes.process="*X-Rise-To-The-Trinny*" OR (Processes.process_name IN ("curl.exe","curl","wget.exe","wget") AND Processes.process="*trin.tar.gz*" AND Processes.process="*--data-binary*")) by Processes.dest Processes.user Processes.process Processes.parent_process_name | `drop_dm_object_name(Processes)`] | convert ctime(firstTime) ctime(lastTime)
| tstats summariesonly=false count min(_time) as firstTime max(_time) as lastTime values(All_Traffic.src) as src values(All_Traffic.dest) as dest from datamodel=Network_Traffic.All_Traffic where (All_Traffic.dest="*skyhanni.cloud" OR All_Traffic.dest_host="*skyhanni.cloud" OR All_Traffic.url="*skyhanni.cloud*" OR All_Traffic.dest_host="igotnofriendsonlineorirl-imgonnakmslmao.skyhanni.cloud") by All_Traffic.dest_host All_Traffic.app All_Traffic.user | `drop_dm_object_name(All_Traffic)` | append [| tstats summariesonly=false count from datamodel=Endpoint.Processes where (Processes.process="*X-Rise-To-The-Trinny*" OR (Processes.process_name IN ("curl.exe","curl","wget.exe","wget") AND Processes.process="*trin.tar.gz*" AND Processes.process="*--data-binary*")) by Processes.dest Processes.user Processes.process Processes.parent_process_name | `drop_dm_object_name(Processes)`] | convert ctime(firstTime) ctime(lastTime)
Beaconing — periodic outbound to small set of destinations Command & Control Medium
C2 channel detection via inter-beacon-time stddev / fan-out to single dest.
ATT&CKT1071.001 T1071.004
Data sourcesNetwork_Traffic.All_Traffic DeviceNetworkEvents
DeviceNetworkEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(1d)
| where RemoteIPType == "Public" and ActionType == "ConnectionSuccess"
| project DeviceName, RemoteIP, RemotePort, Timestamp
| sort by DeviceName asc, RemoteIP asc, RemotePort asc, Timestamp asc
| extend prev_dev = prev(DeviceName, 1), prev_ip = prev(RemoteIP, 1),
         prev_port = prev(RemotePort, 1), prev_ts = prev(Timestamp, 1)
| where DeviceName == prev_dev and RemoteIP == prev_ip and RemotePort == prev_port
| extend delta_sec = datetime_diff('second', Timestamp, prev_ts)
| summarize conn_count = count(), avg_delta = avg(delta_sec), stdev_delta = stdev(delta_sec)
    by DeviceName, RemoteIP, RemotePort
| where conn_count > 30 and avg_delta between (30.0 .. 600.0) and stdev_delta < 5.0
| order by conn_count desc
ImNetworkSession
| where TimeGenerated > ago(2h)
| where DvcAction != "Block"
| where ipv4_is_private(DstIpAddr) == false
| summarize ConnCount = count(),
            DistinctMinutes = dcount(bin(TimeGenerated, 1m))
            by DvcHostname, DstIpAddr, DstPortNumber
| where ConnCount > 50 and DistinctMinutes > 30   // sustained, not bursty
| order by ConnCount desc
NETWORK
Toggle if your env has no CIM data-model acceleration.
| tstats `summariesonly` count, values(All_Traffic.dest_port) AS ports
    from datamodel=Network_Traffic.All_Traffic
    where All_Traffic.action="allowed" AND All_Traffic.dest_category!="internal"
    by _time span=10s, All_Traffic.src, All_Traffic.dest
| `drop_dm_object_name(All_Traffic)`
| streamstats current=f last(_time) AS prev_time by src, dest
| eval delta = _time - prev_time
| stats avg(delta) AS avg_delta stdev(delta) AS sd_delta count by src, dest
| where count > 30 AND sd_delta < 5 AND avg_delta>=30 AND avg_delta<=600
| sort - count
| tstats summariesonly=false count, values(All_Traffic.dest_port) AS ports
    from datamodel=Network_Traffic.All_Traffic
    where All_Traffic.action="allowed" AND All_Traffic.dest_category!="internal"
    by _time span=10s, All_Traffic.src, All_Traffic.dest
| `drop_dm_object_name(All_Traffic)`
| streamstats current=f last(_time) AS prev_time by src, dest
| eval delta = _time - prev_time
| stats avg(delta) AS avg_delta stdev(delta) AS sd_delta count by src, dest
| where count > 30 AND sd_delta < 5 AND avg_delta>=30 AND avg_delta<=600
| sort - count
Network connections to article IPs / domains Command & Control High
Outbound traffic to attacker infrastructure named in the article.
ATT&CKT1071
Data sourcesNetwork_Traffic.All_Traffic Web Network_Resolution.DNS DeviceNetworkEvents
DeviceNetworkEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(7d)
| where RemoteIP in ("") or RemoteUrl has_any ("igotnofriendsonlineorirl-imgonnakmslmao.skyhanni.cloud")
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, ActionType, RemoteIP, RemotePort, RemoteUrl,
          InitiatingProcessFileName, InitiatingProcessCommandLine
let BadIPs     = dynamic([""]);
let BadDomains = dynamic(["igotnofriendsonlineorirl-imgonnakmslmao.skyhanni.cloud"]);
ImNetworkSession

| where DstIpAddr in (BadIPs)
   or Url has_any (BadDomains)

| order by TimeGenerated desc

OAuth consent / suspicious app grant Actions on Objectives High
Cloud identity abuse: app gets high-priv scopes, often via consent phishing.
ATT&CKT1528 T1098.001
Data sourcesAuthentication.Authentication CloudAppEvents
CloudAppEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(7d)

| project Timestamp, AccountObjectId, AccountDisplayName, ActivityType,
          ActivityObjects, IPAddress, UserAgent

AuditLogs

File hash IOCs — endpoint file/process match Installation High
Match SHA256/SHA1/MD5 named in the article against EDR file/process telemetry.
ATT&CKT1027
Data sourcesEndpoint.Filesystem Endpoint.Processes DeviceFileEvents DeviceProcessEvents
// Pre-filter each table BEFORE the union — the engine cannot push
// predicates across `union`, and DeviceFileEvents lacks ProcessCommandLine
// (Initiating only) so column-projection has to differ per side.
union
    ( DeviceFileEvents
        | where Timestamp > ago(7d)
        | where InitiatingProcessAccountName !endswith "$"
        | where SHA256 in~ ("31ecc5939de6d24cf60c50d4ca26cf7a8c322db82a8ce4bd122ebd89cf634255", "b1e4b1f3aad0d489ab0e9208031c67402bbb8480") or SHA1 in~ ("31ecc5939de6d24cf60c50d4ca26cf7a8c322db82a8ce4bd122ebd89cf634255", "b1e4b1f3aad0d489ab0e9208031c67402bbb8480") or MD5 in~ ("31ecc5939de6d24cf60c50d4ca26cf7a8c322db82a8ce4bd122ebd89cf634255", "b1e4b1f3aad0d489ab0e9208031c67402bbb8480")
        | project Timestamp, DeviceName, ActionType, FileName, FolderPath, SHA256,
                  Cmd = InitiatingProcessCommandLine, Source = "DeviceFileEvents" ),
    ( DeviceProcessEvents
        | where Timestamp > ago(7d)
        | where AccountName !endswith "$"
        | where SHA256 in~ ("31ecc5939de6d24cf60c50d4ca26cf7a8c322db82a8ce4bd122ebd89cf634255", "b1e4b1f3aad0d489ab0e9208031c67402bbb8480") or SHA1 in~ ("31ecc5939de6d24cf60c50d4ca26cf7a8c322db82a8ce4bd122ebd89cf634255", "b1e4b1f3aad0d489ab0e9208031c67402bbb8480") or MD5 in~ ("31ecc5939de6d24cf60c50d4ca26cf7a8c322db82a8ce4bd122ebd89cf634255", "b1e4b1f3aad0d489ab0e9208031c67402bbb8480")
        | project Timestamp, DeviceName, ActionType, FileName, FolderPath, SHA256,
                  Cmd = ProcessCommandLine, Source = "DeviceProcessEvents" )
| order by Timestamp desc

// Pre-filter both ASIM tables before the union — same pattern as the
// Defender version so the engine can push hash predicates per-side.
let BadHashes = dynamic(["31ecc5939de6d24cf60c50d4ca26cf7a8c322db82a8ce4bd122ebd89cf634255", "b1e4b1f3aad0d489ab0e9208031c67402bbb8480"]);
union
    ( ImFileEvent
        | where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
        | where ActorUsername !endswith "$"
        | where TargetFileSHA256 in~ (BadHashes)
           or TargetFileSHA1 in~ (BadHashes)
           or TargetFileMD5 in~ (BadHashes)
        | project TimeGenerated, DvcHostname, EventType,
                  TargetFileName, TargetFilePath, TargetFileSHA256,
                  Cmd = ActingProcessName, Source = "ImFileEvent" ),
    ( ImProcessCreate
        | where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
        | where ActorUsername !endswith "$"
        | where SHA256 in~ (BadHashes) or SHA1 in~ (BadHashes) or MD5 in~ (BadHashes)
        | project TimeGenerated, DvcHostname, EventType = TargetProcessName,
                  TargetFileName = TargetProcessName, TargetFilePath = TargetProcessName,
                  TargetFileSHA256 = SHA256,
                  Cmd = TargetProcessCommandLine, Source = "ImProcessCreate" )
| order by TimeGenerated desc

Qinglong task scheduler RCE vulnerabilities exploited in the wild for cryptomining

Snyk
2026-04-27 9 use cases 1 technique 6 kill-chain phases detected

Two authentication bypass vulnerabilities (CVE-2026-3965, CVE-2026-4047) in the Qinglong task scheduling panel were exploited in the wild to deploy cryptomining malware. Here's what happened, how the attacks worked, and what self-hosted application operators should learn from this incident.

Reconnaissance. Attacker researches the target — OSINT, scanning, enumeration. → Asset exposure — vulnerability matches article CVE(s)
Weaponization. Coupling exploit code with deliverable payload (e.g. weaponized PDF/Office doc, trojanized installer).
Delivery. Transmitting the weapon (phishing email, USB, watering hole, drive-by, malicious ad). → [LLM] Qinglong cryptominer payload download from file.551911.xyz
Exploitation. Triggering the exploit — vulnerability/macro/trust abuse to execute code. → [LLM] Qinglong CVE-2026-3965 auth bypass via /open/user/init credential reset · [LLM] Qinglong CVE-2026-4047 case-mismatch auth bypass via /aPi/system/command-run · Article-specific behavioural hunt — Qinglong task scheduler RCE vulnerabilities exploited in the wild for cryptomini
Installation. Establishing persistence on the host — backdoor, service, scheduled task, registry key. → [LLM] Hidden .fullgc cryptominer binary written to /ql/data/db/ · [LLM] Qinglong .fullgc cryptominer execution with nohup backgrounding · Scheduled task created with suspicious image / encoded args
Command & Control. Beacon to attacker infrastructure for control and tasking. → Network connections to article IPs / domains
Actions on Objectives. Lateral movement, credential dumping, data theft, ransomware, sabotage.
Qinglong CVE-2026-3965 auth bypass via /open/user/init credential reset AIExploitation High
Detects unauthenticated PUT requests to the Qinglong /open/user/init endpoint that reinitialize admin credentials by abusing the Express.js rewrite from /open/* to /api/$1. Hunts the article's exact exploitation request at the reverse-proxy / WAF layer where HTTP path is visible. Rationale: Anchors on the article's exact curl proof-of-concept (PUT http://target:5700/open/user/init) and the Express.js rewrite rule documented in Issue #2933. Cross-checked against the Snyk vulnerability DB entry SNYK-JS-WHYOURQINGLONG-15440732 and GitHub issues #2933 / #2924; the /open/* -> /api/$1 rewrite is the structural primitive and is only legitimately used by anonymous endpoints (login, ping) — never /user/init. Cross-checked against: • https://github.com/whyour/qinglong/issues/2933 • https://github.com/whyour/qinglong/pull/2941 • https://security.snyk.io/vuln/SNYK-JS-WHYOURQINGLONG-15440732
ATT&CKT1190 T1556
Data sourcesWeb.Web
Expected false positives · estimated rate: low — model-assessed, tune to your environment
  • Legitimate first-boot Qinglong setup hitting /open/user/init during the install wizard
  • Internal blue-team / scanner replay of the published PoC for patch verification
  • Synthetic monitor probing the init endpoint to confirm availability
  • An admin re-running the init flow after factory-resetting the container
Suppression filter
// Sentinel — exclude internal scanner / synthetic monitors and tag known admin source IPs
| where SourceIP !in ("10.10.20.5","10.10.20.6") // synthetic monitor IPs — replace with env
| where RequestClientApplication !has_any ("Nessus","Qualys","Tenable","OpenVAS")
Response runbook
Step 1 (triage): pull the SourceIP / RequestClientApplication from the WAF hit, confirm whether the host is a known Qinglong instance, and check whether `qinglong` version is <=2.20.1 (vulnerable). Step 2 (contain): block the SourceIP at the perimeter, force-restart the Qinglong container with QL_ENABLE_TWO_FACTOR=true and rotate the admin credential; if PR #2941 not yet applied, take the panel off the public internet (VPN/SSH-tunnel only). Step 3 (hunt): pivot on the same SourceIP for follow-on /api/system/command-run, /api/crons modifications, DNS queries to file.551911.xyz, and file writes under /ql/data/db/.fullgc within the next 24h.
// Defender XDR cannot observe inbound HTTP request paths to a Linux container app.
// Pivot to follow-on artefact: node (qinglong) process spawning a shell that touches
// the admin auth/config layer shortly after exploitation, OR the Qinglong app restarting
// unexpectedly (config.sh write triggers restart per article).
DeviceProcessEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(7d)
| where InitiatingProcessFileName in~ ("node","node.exe","pm2","ts-node")
| where InitiatingProcessCommandLine has_any ("qinglong","/ql/build","/ql/src","@whyour/qinglong")
| where FileName in~ ("sh","bash","dash","ash")
| where ProcessCommandLine has_any ("user/init","/open/user","config.sh","auth.db","db/auth")
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, AccountName, FileName, ProcessCommandLine, InitiatingProcessFileName, InitiatingProcessCommandLine, InitiatingProcessParentFileName
| order by Timestamp desc

(@http.method:PUT OR @http.method:POST) @http.url_details.path:"/open/user/init"

Qinglong CVE-2026-4047 case-mismatch auth bypass via /aPi/system/command-run AIExploitation High
Detects requests to Qinglong /system/command-run where the URL path uses any mixed-case variant of /api/ (e.g. /aPi/, /Api/, /API/). The middleware uses case-sensitive startsWith('/api/') while Express routes case-insensitively, bypassing auth while still reaching the command-execution endpoint. Rationale: Anchors on the article's verbatim PoC (curl -X PUT 'http://target:5700/aPi/system/command-run') and the case-mismatch primitive described in Issue #2934 — middleware does req.path.startsWith('/api/') while Express routes case-insensitively. Regex /(?i)/api/ combined with negative filter on lowercase /api/ catches every mixed-case bypass without false-positive on the legitimate path. Cross-checked Snyk DB SNYK-JS-WHYOURQINGLONG-15468374 and PR #2941 (the real fix at the middleware layer). Cross-checked against: • https://github.com/whyour/qinglong/issues/2934 • https://github.com/whyour/qinglong/pull/2941 • https://security.snyk.io/vuln/SNYK-JS-WHYOURQINGLONG-15468374
ATT&CKT1190 T1059.004
Data sourcesWeb.Web Endpoint.Processes
Expected false positives · estimated rate: low — model-assessed, tune to your environment
  • Vulnerability scanner (Tenable/Qualys/Nessus) replaying the public PoC against an internal Qinglong instance
  • Internal CTF / red-team exercise targeting a sandboxed Qinglong instance
  • Buggy client library emitting case-randomised URLs (very rare in practice — Express convention is all-lowercase)
  • Patch-validation traffic from a maintenance workstation after upgrading to >=2.20.2
Suppression filter
// Sentinel — strip known scanners and patch-validation IPs
| where RequestClientApplication !has_any ("Nessus","Qualys","Tenable","OpenVAS","Nuclei","ZAP")
| where SourceIP !in ("10.10.20.5","10.10.20.6") // patch-validation hosts — replace per env
Response runbook
Step 1 (triage): confirm the target host runs Qinglong <=2.20.1; pull the full RequestURL and the SourceIP / User-Agent; map the SourceIP against known scanner ranges. Step 2 (contain): block the SourceIP at the WAF/perimeter, immediately upgrade Qinglong past PR #2941 (>=2.20.2), audit /ql/config/config.sh and /ql/data/db for tampering, and rotate any credentials stored in the panel. Step 3 (hunt): for the same victim host, query for outbound DNS to file.551911.xyz, file writes to /ql/data/db/.fullgc, and any process named .fullgc launched with nohup; pivot on the SourceIP across the estate for other Qinglong / open Express panels hit with the same case-mismatch technique.
// Detects the qinglong node process spawning a shell with attacker-supplied command
// when CVE-2026-4047 is exploited against /aPi/system/command-run.
DeviceProcessEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(7d)
| where InitiatingProcessFileName in~ ("node","node.exe","pm2","ts-node")
| where InitiatingProcessCommandLine has_any ("qinglong","/ql/build","/ql/src","@whyour/qinglong")
| where FileName in~ ("sh","bash","dash","ash","curl","wget")
| where ProcessCommandLine has_any ("curl","wget","file.551911.xyz","/ql/data/db/.fullgc","nohup","chmod +x","$(uname","-fsSL")
  or ProcessCommandLine matches regex @"(?i)>\s*/dev/null\s+2>&1\s+&"
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, AccountName, FileName, ProcessCommandLine, InitiatingProcessFileName, InitiatingProcessCommandLine, InitiatingProcessParentFileName, SHA256
| order by Timestamp desc
// Primary: WAF / reverse-proxy logs ingested via CommonSecurityLog
let MixedCaseApi = CommonSecurityLog
| where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
| where RequestURL matches regex @"/(?i:api)/(?:system/command-run|system/run-script|crons)"
| where RequestURL !contains "/api/" // exclude the all-lowercase legitimate path
| project TimeGenerated, SourceIP, DestinationHostName, DestinationPort, RequestURL, RequestMethod, RequestClientApplication, DeviceVendor, DeviceProduct;
// Secondary: Nginx access logs forwarded via Syslog
let NginxMixedCase = Syslog
| where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
| where ProcessName has_any ("nginx","openresty","caddy","traefik")
| where SyslogMessage matches regex @"/(?i:api)/(?:system/command-run|system/run-script|crons)"
| where SyslogMessage !contains "/api/"
| project TimeGenerated, Computer, HostIP, ProcessName, SyslogMessage;
// Tertiary: ASIM process telemetry — qinglong spawning a shell with attacker payload markers
let QinglongShell = ImProcessCreate
| where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
| where ParentProcessName has_any ("node","pm2","ts-node")
| where ParentProcessCommandLine has_any ("qinglong","/ql/build","/ql/src","@whyour/qinglong")
| where ActingProcessName has_any ("sh","bash","dash","curl","wget")
| where ActingProcessCommandLine has_any ("file.551911.xyz","/ql/data/db/.fullgc","nohup","chmod +x","$(uname")
| project TimeGenerated, DvcHostname, ActorUsername, ActingProcessName, ActingProcessCommandLine, ParentProcessName, ParentProcessCommandLine;
union MixedCaseApi, NginxMixedCase, QinglongShell
| order by TimeGenerated desc
